answer.evidence: The object is a front-on view of a staircase going down. It is a stack of horizontal bands: a beam (rows 0-2), a stone strip (3-5), another beam (6-8), a dark void (9-12), then step risers at rows 13-15, 17-19, 21-25 and 27-31. Each step has only a 1-row lighter edge line (rows 13, 17, 21, 26) above a flat face, with no tread plane. Widths are constant at 44 px apart from the strip at rows 3-5. No step shows a horizontal tread of 3 or more rows and there is no ellipse or roof. This is vertical elevation, not a flat plate and not a 3/4 top view. It is a structure rather than a flat floor decal, so the kind plausibly does not match.

styleAnswer.evidence: The stairwell is a small floor feature: a wooden frame around a descending flight. The dark edge pixels are tinted dark brown beside the wood, with 0% near-neutral, so the outline is dark_material_tone rather than a black sticker line. The measured 9 visible tones per tile beat the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7), and near-flat coverage is 0%. By eye, the frame has a light top rail, mid wood and a dark underside. The steps alternate lit treads and darker risers, fading to a deep shadow at the top, which gives about 5 brown ramp steps. Texture is more restrained than the paving's per-stone shading, since the steps are mostly clean bands and the frame is smooth. There are no large single-colour fills, though, and a careful artist would accept it beside the references without it looking thinner or flatter.
